title: $T_{E,\Qlb}$ on bounded constructible complexes
statement:
For a prime $\ell$, a scheme $X$ and a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$, the
functor

$$
T_{E,\Qlb}\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)
$$

between the categories of [def-sfb-dcons-subfield] and [def-sfb-dcons-qlbar] is the restriction
of the derived extension of scalars of [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], which preserves
bounded constructible complexes by [lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible].

Explicitly, an object $K$ is sent to $T_{E,\Qlb}K$, with its bounded constructibility
supplied by [lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible]. For a morphism $f\colon K\to L$,
the image is the image of $f$ under the ambient functor of
[def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]. The source and target have the ambient morphisms
because they are the full subcategories in [def-sfb-dcons-subfield] and
[def-sfb-dcons-qlbar].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-ND-2c058642d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and changed nothing. Shape: one commit holding the item and its report, with no new nodes and no change to the unit. The first paragraph of the item matches the main-20261015 blueprint node (order 1767) word for word: prime ℓ, scheme X, finite extension E/Q_ℓ inside Q̄_ℓ, and the functor D_cons(X,E)→D_cons(X,Q̄_ℓ) obtained by restricting the derived extension of scalars. The added paragraph only spells out what restricting to full subcategories means for objects and morphisms. Each of the four cited statements says what the item takes from it. def-sfb-dcons-subfield is the full subcategory of D(Mod_{E_X}), where E_X is the pullback p_X^* of the condensed ring of E with the topology restricted from Q̄_ℓ. def-sfb-dcons-qlbar is the full subcategory of D(Mod_{Q̄_ℓ,X}). def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar is the derived extension along def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map; following that through j_E (def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-to-qlbar) back to def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring gives the same E_X, the same module-object category and the same derived category as the source of def-sfb-dcons-subfield. This settles the earlier return L. lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible gives exactly the object condition, under the same hypotheses (ℓ, X, E). Both coefficient categories use sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible with no completeness condition, so no two different coefficient categories are identified. There is no cycle: the lemma's proof dependencies do not include the item. Edge cases checked: X empty, K = 0, E = Q_ℓ, and a field-valued point. No duplicates: def-sfb-constructible-extend-subfield has a finite target F, while def-sfb-constructible-extend-comp-iso and def-sfb-constructible-cocone are built on this item. The item covers the restriction clause of the unit paragraph 'The cocone itself'. It is not the unit's key node, so leaving `realized` untouched is right. No other-unit statements are cited, no tool_uses are needed and there is no SGA citation. Six Mathlib searches of all three kinds are recorded with no match. The archived upstream TwoColimit.lean that the report quotes is not on this machine, so I could not check that quote; it is reference material only and the definition does not depend on it.
